summary: @servicetitan/cp-react-hooks ships preinstall dropper that runs obfuscated payload under a downloaded Bun runtime
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (identifier names `_0xNNNN`, string-array rotation) and downloads the Bun runtime zip from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, extracts it, chmod+x's the bun binary in a temp directory, and invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`. The file math_init.js is a 727KB single-line Bun-CJS module (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with a custom string-array + numeric-index decoder (`WV8StW` rotator over base64-like alphabet) and fully renamed identifiers. math_init.js is not listed in package.json's `files` array (which declares only `dist` and `src`), so it is an undeclared blob smuggled into the published tarball. Fetching a second language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated, undeclared payload has no relationship to the package's advertised purpose (a React hooks library) and evades Node-based inspection. The package is published on the public npm registry under the `@servicetitan/*` scope, a namespace commonly used for that vendor's private packages, consistent with a dependency-confusion attempt against internal build systems that resolve the public registry ahead of an internal one.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
